context: Evaluates whether the agent correctly identifies a pick-one layer redundancy and cites the layer's cardinality and note field as the reasoning, rather than a vague impression of duplication. Covers Workflow step 4's redundancy check and the cardinality-not-preference mindset.

checklist.name: Both tools mapped to the layer
checklist.description: graphnav and codelantern are both identified as mapping to the Code Navigation layer

checklist.name: Redundancy finding raised
checklist.description: The response raises a redundancy finding for the two tools sharing a layer

checklist.name: Cardinality named explicitly
checklist.description: The finding names the layer's cardinality value, pick-one, explicitly

checklist.name: Note field cited as reasoning
checklist.description: The layer's note field is quoted or closely paraphrased as the reason two active tools conflict

checklist.name: No vague duplication language in place of the field
checklist.description: The finding is not justified only by a general impression such as seems duplicative, in place of citing cardinality and note

checklist.name: Drop verdict surfaced separately
checklist.description: codelantern's drop verdict is raised as an additional, distinct reason to remove it

checklist.name: Dataset freshness reported
checklist.description: meta.last_updated or an equivalent freshness statement appears in the response

checklist.name: No silent edit
checklist.description: Neither .mcp.json entry is edited or removed by the agent in this turn

checklist.name: Findings presented as a list
checklist.description: Findings are presented as a list for the user to act on, not folded into a single vague paragraph
